findings.claim: process_events deduplicates on event kind instead of event id, so a distinct event whose kind was already seen in the call is dropped.
evidence: test_events.py:13,18 use only one-id-per-kind inputs, so the suite passes despite the defect (merged tests-1)
findings.failure_mechanism: two distinct events (different ids) share a kind -> the second one's kind is already in handled, so it is skipped -> distinct event never reaches the handler: I1 and R1/A1 are violated (silent data loss)

findings.claim: Dedup tracks kind, never id, so distinct events sharing a kind are dropped (I1/A1).
findings.failure_mechanism: id=1/created then id=2/created -> second skipped -> distinct event dropped
findings.rejection_reason: Same root cause as invariants-1 (dedup keyed on kind); merged there.

findings.claim: A redelivery that repeats the id but carries a different kind is passed to handler again.
findings.failure_mechanism: same id redelivered with a changed kind -> kind not in handled -> handler called again
findings.severity_change_reason: rejected at gate step 2 and merged at step 6
findings.rejection_reason: The contract defines a redelivery as a repeat of the same event (same id), so a redelivery with a changed kind is speculation outside the contract. The real defect is the wrong dedup key, which invariants-1 already records.

findings.claim: No test covers distinct ids that share a kind, so the kind-keyed dedup survives the suite.

findings.rejection_reason: Under the test-strength rule, a test that cannot fail while its requirement is broken is evidence of the code defect. Its evidence is kept in invariants-1.
